rows.internal_claim: Connected Cartesian product structure has a factor decomposition, and product automorphisms are controlled by prime-factor automorphisms together with permutations of isomorphic factors.
rows.external_boundary: Sabidussi–Vizing unique factorization and the classical Cartesian-product automorphism theory already provide the product-level rigidity. The exact P000 Cell typing is not part of the classical theorem.

rows.internal_claim: W=(S3 x S3) semidirect C2 ≅ S3 wr S2 is the full whole-block-preserving motion envelope for two interchangeable 3-axis blocks; |W|=72.
rows.external_boundary: This is the standard equal-block partition stabilizer in S6. It also appears exactly as Aut(H(2,3))=S3 wr S2.

rows.internal_claim: b=(E2 E4)(E3 E5), fixing E1,E6, is outside W because it maps the A-block to a mixed 3-set rather than a whole block.
rows.external_boundary: Membership in a partition stabilizer is classical. The finite checker verifies b∉W for the task labels.

rows.internal_claim: The current product adjacency, in which one factor changes while the other is fixed, is not preserved by the target partial cross-factor coordinate mixer.
rows.external_boundary: Classical Cartesian-product theory says automorphisms respect prime-factor/layer structure up to whole permutations of isomorphic factors. This supports the product-level obstruction. The exact P000 adjacency/relation typing and the particular six-axis relabel are project-instance data.

rows.internal_claim: Closure under composition, inverse and legal restriction of the currently supplied block-preserving relations cannot manufacture a genuinely mixed-support relation.
rows.external_boundary: Closure of total block-preserving permutations stays inside the partition stabilizer, and restriction of supplied partial bijections stays a partial symmetry of supplied maps. The P000 support type and Cell-valued relation grammar are project-specific.

rows.internal_claim: Renaming the current laws as partial/groupoid arrows does not by itself create a missing mixed-domain relation object.
rows.external_boundary: In standard partial-action/inverse-semigroup formalisms the domains and partial bijections/isomorphisms are explicit data. Partiality can represent a new cross-block arrow if one is supplied, but does not canonically infer that arrow from block-pure generators.

rows.internal_claim: A richer local/fibered relation structure could support mixed-coordinate transport without treating the state as a direct product.
rows.external_boundary: Cartesian graph bundles are a standard generalization of graph products/coverings and can carry transition data between fibers. This is a design analogy only, not an identification with P000 BMix_b.

rows.internal_claim: Adding the target b as a new global total axis permutation on top of the full W envelope is not a safe minimal extension.
rows.external_boundary: Because W=S3 wr S2 is a maximal imprimitive subgroup of S6 and b∉W, group theory forces <W,b>=S6. The checker independently enumerates all 720 elements. Thus a global-permutation extension automatically admits arbitrary S6 axis permutations.

rows.internal_claim: A non-S6-collapsing BMix_b must be typed/partial/domain-sensitive or otherwise relation-level, with explicit source/target/support/payload semantics.
rows.external_boundary: Partial actions, inverse semigroups and graph bundles are standard tool families for typed/local transformations. None of the audited sources determines the P000-minimal relation or proves Cell/stack/handle consistency.

rows.internal_claim: Carrier/readout equivalence, product representation or external quotient equivalence must not identify distinct P000 native states.
rows.external_boundary: This is an internal ontology/operation-safety guard. Classical product decomposition and partial-symmetry theories do not prescribe the P000 native identity relation.
